note: Every entry was verified against an article opened during research; incidentDate and publishedDate are separate. Names of private individuals and minors are withheld.

items.headline: Supreme Court rejects review of its December 2013 ruling criminalising gay sex
items.summary: A bench of Justices HL Dattu and SJ Mukhopadhaya dismissed petitions by the federal government, the Naz Foundation and others seeking review of the 11 December 2013 verdict. Al Jazeera described it as a setback to gay rights groups.
items.outcome: Review petitions dismissed; curative petitions followed.

items.headline: HRW urges India to enforce 2014 Supreme Court ruling on transgender rights
items.summary: Human Rights Watch said authorities should fully enforce the April 2014 NALSA judgment recognising a 'third gender' and called for credible investigation of recent incidents in which police allegedly abused transgender people. It said stigma and discrimination continued despite the ruling.

items.headline: Supreme Court recognises transgender people as a third gender (NALSA)
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported the court recognised a third gender and called recognition 'a human rights issue'. It directed state and federal governments to identify transgender people as a third gender with access to welfare schemes.
items.outcome: Landmark ruling; directions to governments on welfare and recognition.

items.headline: India gets its first transgender news anchor on Coimbatore channel
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that Padmini Prakash, 31, read her first bulletin on Lotus TV in Coimbatore. She said she had dropped out of college after her family abandoned her at 18.

items.headline: Hyderabad trans activists demand arrest of man accused in 2015 murder of trans woman
items.summary: Scroll reported that a man arrested in February 2015 for the murder of a trans woman was granted bail eight months later, and that community group Sampoorna launched an online campaign alleging assaults on trans women since 2012. The allegations were made by activists.
items.outcome: Accused out on bail at time of report.

items.headline: West Bengal appoints India's first transgender college principal
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported a transgender woman was appointed principal of Krishnagar Women's College, according to the chairman of the state panel that selects principals. He said she had taught in college for more than 20 years.

items.headline: Man attending Mumbai LGBTQI forum assaulted by gang; FIR filed nine days later
items.summary: The News Minute reported a participant was molested and then assaulted by a group of men near the venue. An FIR was registered at Khar police station invoking general assault sections, with six accused booked.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu gets first transgender woman police sub-inspector
items.summary: The News Minute reported Prithika Yashini received her appointment order from the Salem Police Commissioner among 21 new sub-inspectors. It said the Madras High Court had earlier directed the recruitment board to include a 'third category'.

items.headline: Mumbai: one of two women dies after family forbade them from meeting
items.summary: Scroll reported that after a father found out about the relationship and forbade his daughter from seeing a neighbour, she attempted suicide and survived, while the other woman died, police said. LGBT groups described it as part of a pattern.

items.headline: Three transgender persons allege beating by Thrissur police, file complaint
items.summary: Two of the three filed a complaint with the district police chief alleging that a three-member team including a sub-inspector beat them with a cane. They said there was no provocation.

items.headline: Lucknow holds its first Queer Pride Parade
items.summary: Scroll reported about 300 people marched 1.5 km from Sikandarbagh crossing to Hazratganj GPO, some from as far as Mumbai, Chandigarh, Jaipur and Kolkata.

items.headline: Kochi Metro hires 23 transgender persons
items.summary: Scroll reported the agency's managing director said it was the first government-owned company in India to formally appoint them, with posts in housekeeping, ticketing, customer relations and other roles.

items.headline: Joyita Mondal, India's first transgender judge, calls for job reservation
items.summary: PTI reported Joyita Mondal, described as India's first transgender judge, urged reservations in government jobs and more shelter homes for the community. Another report said West Bengal appointed her to a Lok Adalat in July 2017.

items.headline: Kerala trans community reports string of attacks despite state transgender policy
items.summary: Scroll reported that activists counted 10 allegedly transphobic attacks, including a murder, in seven months since July 2017, despite Kerala launching a state transgender policy in 2015. Activists said the policy would only work if police and the public are sensitised.

items.headline: Fifteen transgender persons in Kochi allege police beating; six booked
items.summary: The News Minute reported the group said police beat them at midnight near the KSRTC bus station, while police said they acted on a complaint. Police reportedly registered a case against six under IPC sections on dacoity and obscenity; some of the group worked at Kochi Metro.
items.outcome: Six booked; community federation to complain to DGP.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds right to privacy; HRW says ruling gives hope to LGBT community
items.summary: A nine-judge bench unanimously held privacy a fundamental right. HRW noted the judges criticised an earlier verdict that treated the LGBT community as 'minuscule', saying Section 377 had a chilling effect on sexual orientation as an element of privacy and dignity.
items.outcome: Section 377 case referred to a larger bench.

items.headline: Varanasi college student expelled from hostel amid rumours she is lesbian
items.summary: The Wire reported a student of a BHU-affiliated women's college was allegedly expelled from her hostel over rumours; the college said she had been harassing other students. The student denied the claims and Scroll reported there was no formal inquiry.

items.headline: Two trans women allege police assault in Kozhikode; Chief Minister orders probe
items.summary: Two transgender women said they were beaten by police patrolling near the railway station at 2.30am on 27 December. Kerala's Chief Minister ordered a probe, the News Minute reported.

items.headline: Mob in Thiruvananthapuram beats trans woman accused of being a child abductor
items.summary: A 27-year-old trans woman was attacked in Valiyathura by residents who accused her of disguising herself as a woman to abduct children. The News Minute said the attack was without any proof and a video of it sparked outrage.

items.headline: After lynching, Hyderabad police relocate trans women and homeless people
items.summary: The News Minute reported that Hyderabad police decided to relocate homeless people and transgender persons to 'safer' locations amid rumour-fuelled mob violence. It said some trans women were being sent to native places and others admitted to shelter homes.

items.headline: Hyderabad police arrest 14 over lynching of transgender person
items.summary: The South Zone police and Commissioner's Task Force arrested 14 people in connection with the 26 May killing of a transgender person at Chandrayangutta. Police said teams were deployed to stop rumours spreading.

items.headline: Transgender woman killed by mob in Hyderabad over child-kidnapping WhatsApp rumours
items.summary: Police said a group of transgender women seeking alms in Chandrayangutta were attacked by a mob that believed, based on WhatsApp forwards, they were a gang out to kidnap children. One of the women died.

items.headline: Feature: victims of extortion and assault on Grindr stay silent for fear of police
items.summary: ThePrint's report, published before the Section 377 verdict, described a man's account of a first date that went wrong. It said victims of sexual abuse and extortion on Grindr often avoid police because homosexuality was then criminalised; the account uses a changed name.

items.headline: Ahmedabad: two women die in Sabarmati river; police report them as a couple
items.summary: PTI reported a lesbian couple, aged 30 and 28, died after jumping into the Sabarmati river, and a three-year-old child also died. Scroll noted at the time that same-sex relationships were still illegal.

items.headline: Assam gets its first transgender judge in Guwahati Lok Adalat
items.summary: Scroll reported Swati Bidhan Baruah, 26, was among 20 member judges to mediate cases in a Lok Adalat in Guwahati. It noted West Bengal and Maharashtra had made similar appointments in 2017 and February 2018.

items.headline: Supreme Court decriminalises consensual same-sex conduct, reading down Section 377
items.summary: A five-judge Constitution bench of the Supreme Court ruled on 6 September 2018 that criminalising consensual same-sex conduct between adults is unconstitutional. Human Rights Watch called it a major victory for privacy and non-discrimination.
items.outcome: Section 377 read down for consensual adult conduct; the 2013 Koushal ruling was overturned.

items.headline: Hyderabad High Court reads down Telangana Eunuchs Act in interim order
items.summary: The interim order was based on a petition by transgender activists who called the century-old law wholly unconstitutional. The News Minute said the Act had given state police arbitrary powers to arrest and prosecute transgender persons.
items.outcome: Act read down in interim order.

items.headline: Kerala High Court reunites lesbian couple separated by one partner's parents
items.summary: Scroll reported that two women who had lived together for about a day on 12 August were forcibly separated by one's parents; the High Court intervened on Monday to reunite them. The couple said they wanted to show same-sex couples can lead normal lives.

items.headline: Trans woman held in men's jail in Ernakulam moved after protests
items.summary: The News Minute reported that police who arrested her did not believe she was a trans woman and lodged her in the men's sub jail. She was moved to a transgender cell at Viyyur Central Jail after friends protested.

items.headline: Trans woman priest killed in Thoothukudi temple; police yet to arrest suspect, activists say
items.summary: A 38-year-old trans woman who served as a temple priest was killed in Thoothukudi district. Police had identified a 23-year-old former temple secretary as the main accused; the report said he was reportedly in a relationship with her earlier.
items.outcome: No arrest at the time of the report.

items.headline: Hyderabad: man accused in 2015 trans woman's murder arrested under Preventive Detention Act
items.summary: The News Minute reported a 28-year-old rowdy-sheeter accused in the 2015 murder of a Hyderabad trans woman was arrested under the Preventive Detention Act after the trans community complained of extortion and attacks. He was accused in 10 cases since 2014, the report said, citing Times of India.
items.outcome: Detained under the Preventive Detention Act, which allows detention for up to a year.

items.headline: Madras High Court: transwoman is a 'bride' under the Hindu Marriage Act
items.summary: The Madurai bench ruled that a 'bride' under the Hindu Marriage Act includes transgender and intersex persons who identify as women. The case was brought by a Tuticorin couple whose marriage registration had been refused.

items.headline: Madras High Court directs Tamil Nadu to ban sex reassignment surgeries on intersex infants
items.summary: The court directed the state to ban such surgeries on intersex infants and children, in an order recognising their human rights. Activist Gopi Shankar called it a historic verdict across Asia.

items.headline: Video shows Salem police inspector beating 26-year-old trans woman; inquiry ordered
items.summary: The News Minute reported a viral video showing an inspector striking a trans woman with a lathi on Omalur Main Road, with two other officers present. The Salem Commissioner ordered an inquiry against the inspector, according to later reporting in the same article.

items.headline: HRW: LGBT youth in India face bullying and drop out of school
items.summary: HRW wrote that many LGBT youth face harassment and bullying and often skip classes or leave school. It said most teachers are not trained to respond, and in some cases participate in harassment, citing two reports published that month.

items.headline: Video shows UP police beating transgender people inside Meerut station
items.summary: The Wire reported a video showing officers striking members of the transgender community inside Lal Kurti police station. Officials said action was taken after the group fought another group over distribution of collected 'gifts'.

items.headline: Many trans employees quit Kochi Metro, with 11 of 43 still working, report says
items.summary: The News Minute reported that only 11 of 43 trans persons employed through the social inclusion initiative remained, with some workers describing it as a PR gimmick. The report is based on interviews with former staff.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu issues order banning unnecessary surgery on intersex children
items.summary: HRW reported the state issued an executive order banning genital surgeries on children with intersex variations except in 'life-threatening situations'. The order also warns against misusing that clause.

items.headline: Rajya Sabha passes Transgender Persons Bill despite community opposition
items.summary: The News Minute reported the House voted down a motion to send the bill to a Select Committee, 70 to 55. It said the trans community had rejected the Bill as regressive.

items.headline: Transgender Persons Act receives presidential assent despite community protests
items.summary: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act received President's assent on 5 December 2019. The News Minute reported that transgender communities and allies had protested, saying the Act treats trans persons as inferior citizens and contravenes the 2014 NALSA judgment on self-determination.

items.headline: Mumbai Police deny permission for annual queer pride march, citing fear of anti-CAA slogans
items.summary: Police said they had information that placards and slogans criticising the CAA and NRC might be used. The march by Queer Azaadi Mumbai had been scheduled for 1 February at August Kranti Maidan.
items.outcome: Permission later granted on conditions, per Scroll's follow-up.

items.headline: As lockdown begins, trans people warned of heightened poverty and ill health
items.summary: Activists and community members told reporters that many trans people make a living on the streets through sex work and begging and would be among the worst hit by the 21-day lockdown. A Pratyay Gender Trust worker said many lack social safety nets.

items.headline: Two women in Namakkal die by suicide; stigma over relationship suspected
items.summary: The News Minute reported that two women who had worked at a loom unit were fired after the owner disapproved of their friendship and died by suicide. It said it appeared they may have been in a relationship; no note was found.

items.headline: Uttarakhand High Court: same-sex couples cannot marry yet have a right to live together
items.summary: On a habeas corpus petition by a woman whose partner was allegedly detained by her mother and brother, the court said consenting adults of the same gender have a right to live together outside wedlock.

items.headline: Orissa High Court allows same-sex couple to live together on habeas corpus plea
items.summary: A bench allowed a couple to live together after one partner, who identifies as a man under the NALSA judgment, said the other was forcibly separated by her mother in Bhubaneswar. The court also extended protection of the domestic violence law to the woman partner.
items.outcome: Couple allowed to live together; state to provide protection.

items.headline: Centre tells Delhi High Court same-sex marriage is not Indian culture or law
items.summary: The Solicitor General opposed a petition seeking recognition of same-sex marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act. The bench said it needed to examine the petition with an open mind.

items.headline: Kolkata Police official arrested for allegedly harassing transgender activist
items.summary: A police official was arrested after a transgender activist, a member of the state's Transgender Welfare Board, and two women with her complained to Bowbazar police station. Police sources said he allegedly misbehaved after blocking their car.

items.headline: Centre notifies Transgender Persons Rules 2020, no medical exam to declare gender
items.summary: The Social Justice Ministry issued the rules after a draft in July drew criticism from the LGBTQ community. Scroll reported, citing The Indian Express, that trans people no longer need a medical examination to declare their desired sex.

items.headline: Coimbatore police arrest employee over killing of 60-year-old trans woman entrepreneur
items.summary: Police arrested a 23-year-old employee of a trans-run eatery in connection with the killing. The police commissioner cited a 'personal dispute' while a police press release alleged the accused killed her for rejecting his advances.

items.headline: Delhi High Court orders police protection for lesbian woman forcibly married in 2019
items.summary: A 23-year-old woman said she was forcibly married to a man in October 2019 despite her parents knowing her sexual orientation, and was threatened with being 'cured'. Justice Mukta Gupta directed Delhi Police to protect her and said she may move elsewhere.

items.headline: Madras High Court issues guidelines to protect LGBTQIA+ people and curb 'cure' attempts
items.summary: Hearing a lesbian couple's petition for protection from police and family, the court asked the Union government to ban attempts to 'cure or change' sexual orientation and ordered action against health professionals who do so. It also issued guidelines for police handling missing complaints involving consenting adults.
items.outcome: Guidelines issued by a single-judge bench.

items.headline: Karnataka becomes first state to reserve 1% of government jobs for transgender people
items.summary: The state told the High Court it had amended its civil service recruitment rules, with a final notification on 6 July 2021 providing 1% reservation across general and reserved categories. The notification also states there should be no discrimination against trans persons in selection.

items.headline: Kerala's first trans woman radio jockey found dead days after alleging botched surgery
items.summary: A 28-year-old trans woman was found dead in her Kochi apartment, with police saying the death was suspected to be suicide. Days earlier she had alleged medical negligence in her gender-affirming surgery.
items.outcome: Police suspected suicide; the government later ordered a probe (see follow-up).

items.headline: Salem teenager's killing prompts debate on birth-family guardianship for trans youth
items.summary: A 17-year-old transgender girl was killed in Salem district; police arrested her 25-year-old brother, who reportedly said he saw her identity as a shame to the family. The report argued the Transgender Persons Act's reliance on birth families as guardians is risky.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu reconstitutes Transgender Welfare Board with 12 trans members
items.summary: The state reconstituted its welfare board, first formed in 2008, with 12 transgender persons and one cisgender woman, including two trans men. The report said communities appreciated the priority given to trans voices.

items.headline: Kerala High Court tells state to frame guidelines against conversion therapy
items.summary: In an interim order on a petition to ban the practice, the court said stringent action should follow if forced conversion is proved. Guidelines were to be drafted in about five months with LGBTQIA+ groups.
items.outcome: Interim order; state asked to frame guidelines.

items.headline: Salem police arrest mother and five men over death of young trans woman
items.summary: Police said an attack on a young transgender woman in Salem on 13 December was planned by her mother, who allegedly wanted her killed for being transgender. The woman died the next day.
items.outcome: Mother and five men arrested and charged with murder, remanded to judicial custody.

items.headline: Kerala government orders probe into death of trans woman who alleged botched surgery
items.summary: On 24 January 2022 the state government ordered a probe into the July 2021 death of a 28-year-old trans woman, acting on a complaint that the hospital's alleged gross negligence led to the suicide. Police had said she died by suicide.

items.headline: Ahmedabad police arrest three accused of robbing men met on Grindr
items.summary: Police said the three used the gay dating app to find victims, lured them to secluded places and beat and robbed them. An officer said the accused confessed to robbing at least 15 or 20 people in four months.

items.headline: Allahabad High Court rejects two women's plea for recognition of marriage
items.summary: The UP government's counsel opposed the plea, saying same-sex marriage is against Indian culture and invalid under Indian laws. The women had argued the Hindu Marriage Act does not oppose homosexual marriage.

items.headline: Faridabad police bust gang allegedly blackmailing men met via gay dating app
items.summary: Police said three men were arrested for luring men, filming them and robbing them at gunpoint. Two alleged masterminds were absconding at the time.

items.headline: Kerala lesbian couple reunited in High Court after one was taken by family
items.summary: A woman's partner filed a habeas corpus petition after the woman was taken by her family and alleged to have been subjected to conversion therapy. The News Minute reported police at Thamarassery had earlier declined help, calling it a family matter.
items.outcome: The couple, both adults, were reunited in the Kerala High Court on 31 May 2022.

items.headline: Activist alleges Delhi police beat transperson taken from government-supported shelter
items.summary: An activist alleged in a livestream that Dabri police forcibly picked up a trans person from a Garima Greh shelter and beat them. PTI reported the Delhi Police rejected the allegations.

items.headline: National Medical Commission says conversion therapy is professional misconduct
items.summary: In a letter dated 25 August the regulator told state medical councils that conversion therapy to alter sexuality is professional misconduct. The NMC said the Madras High Court had directed it to issue the notification in July.
items.outcome: State councils empowered to act against practitioners.

items.headline: Supreme Court says families can be unmarried partnerships and queer relationships
items.summary: A bench of Justices Chandrachud and Bopanna said such families deserve equal protection under the law as traditional ones, while ruling on a maternity leave case. The ruling did not itself address marriage rights.

items.headline: Five transgender persons attacked at Agartala mall during Durga festivities
items.summary: The Wire reported that heckling escalated into an attack by nearly 40 men on five trans persons at a shopping complex, causing injuries. An FIR was filed at West Agartala Women's Police Station, though the victims alleged police apathy.

items.headline: Delhi police arrest two over stabbing of 22-year-old transgender person
items.summary: Police said two men aged 20 and 21 were arrested with the help of call records and CCTV footage. They said the accused allegedly acted after the victim threatened to disclose their relationship to his father unless paid.

items.headline: Supreme Court stays Kerala High Court order sending lesbian woman for conversion therapy
items.summary: A bench headed by the Chief Justice stayed the order after the woman's partner alleged she was illegally detained by her parents. It issued notice to the state and the parents and sought a report on the factual situation.

items.headline: Kerala trans couple welcome baby at government hospital, described as a first in India
items.summary: PTI reported the baby was born by caesarean section at Government Medical College Hospital in Kozhikode. The couple declined to reveal the newborn's gender identity.

items.headline: Centre tells Supreme Court same-sex marriage pleas reflect 'urban elitist views'
items.summary: ThePrint reported the Union government's application questioned the maintainability of the petitions and said recognition would entail judicial creation of a new social institution. A five-judge bench was to hear the matter on 18 April.
items.outcome: Supreme Court later said there was no data to back the claim.

items.headline: Thane: transgender person killed by live-in partner, police say
items.summary: PTI reported police said a transgender person of about 30 died after a fight with their partner, also a transgender person, in Bhiwandi. A murder case was registered.

items.headline: Kerala trans man and activist's suicide prompts condemnation of media and cyberbullying
items.summary: The News Minute reported that allegations of defamatory news articles and cyberbullying were linked by mourners and officials to his death. The Social Justice Minister condemned what she called irresponsible journalism.

items.headline: Malappuram woman files habeas corpus alleging lesbian partner held by family
items.summary: A 21-year-old woman told the Kerala High Court that her partner's family took her from their workplace on 30 May. The report said the family allegedly did not comply with the court's order to produce her on 9 June.

items.headline: Telangana High Court strikes down colonial-era Eunuchs Act
items.summary: A bench led by Chief Justice Ujjal Bhuyan declared the Telangana Eunuchs Act, 1329 Fasli unconstitutional on 6 July. It directed the state to issue orders on reservation in education and employment and asked the Transgender Welfare Board to monitor steps.
items.outcome: Act struck down; reservation orders directed.

items.headline: Hyderabad police arrest 19 as 'fake' trans women in begging crackdown; activists object
items.summary: The News Minute reported 19 people were arrested in Hyderabad on accusations of posing as transgender women, with extortion charges for begging. The report said the arrests reflected police ignorance of trans identities, a view of the outlet and activists.

items.headline: Kanpur police arrest six over alleged 'sextortion' racket on gay dating app
items.summary: Police said the accused created fake profiles on the app Blued, took victims on dates, filmed them, robbed them and threatened to circulate videos.

items.headline: Kerala High Court refuses parents' plea for surgery on seven-year-old intersex child
items.summary: Justice VG Arun refused permission for genital reconstructive surgery and directed the state to form a multidisciplinary committee and issue an order regulating such surgeries on intersex children.
items.outcome: Surgery permission refused; state directed to regulate.

items.headline: Gujarat High Court seeks report from law university on harassment of queer student
items.summary: The High Court took cognisance of a news report in which a student wrote of being made to feel bad about being queer at Gujarat National Law University. It sought details of the Internal Complaints Committee and issued notice to the registrar.

items.headline: Gurugram police arrest four over extortion using LGBTQ dating app
items.summary: Police said a man befriended on Grindr was allegedly part of a group that assaulted the complainant, took Rs 95,000 and his phone, and threatened to leak private videos. The accused were arrested from Delhi.

items.headline: Bengaluru police arrest two trans women under Karnataka anti-beggary law
items.summary: Sadashiva Nagar police arrested two transgender women on 9 September under Section 11 of the Karnataka Prohibition of Beggary Act. The News Minute described it as arbitrary enforcement of the law.

items.headline: Supreme Court declines to grant legal recognition to same-sex marriage
items.summary: A five-judge Constitution bench led by the Chief Justice declined to read same-sex couples into the Special Marriage Act, with the bench split on whether the state must recognise civil unions. Deccan Herald reported it upheld queer couples' right to cohabit without threat of violence, coercion or interference.
items.outcome: No legal recognition of same-sex marriage; the issue left to Parliament.

items.headline: Parliamentary panel recommends retaining Section 377 in new criminal code; draft had omitted it
items.summary: ThePrint reported the Standing Committee on Home Affairs said it was 'mandatory' to reintroduce Section 377 in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for gender-neutral offences, after the Bill deleted it. Critics have raised concerns about the lack of provisions for male and trans victims of sexual assault.
items.outcome: Recommendation not adopted in the final code, according to later reports.

items.headline: Supreme Court issues notice on plea by trans teacher terminated by two private schools
items.summary: PTI reported the court agreed to hear a transgender woman's plea that her services were terminated by schools in Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh after her gender identity became known. The bench issued notices to the Centre and both states.

items.headline: Chennai: man allegedly kills male partner then dies by suicide after family opposition
items.summary: The News Minute reported that a 24-year-old man allegedly killed his 25-year-old partner at a lodge and then died by suicide, following family pressure over the relationship. The two had met on a dating app and the man had become engaged to a woman after parents learned of it.

items.headline: Kerala: family refuses to claim body of queer man; partner moves High Court
items.summary: The News Minute reported the man was declared dead on 4 February after a fall, and his family refused to pay medical expenses or collect his body. His partner approached the High Court because Indian law does not recognise a partner as legal heir.

items.headline: Supreme Court closes curative petitions against 2013 Section 377 verdict as infructuous
items.summary: A five-judge bench declared the curative petitions against the 2013 judgment infructuous, saying they were rendered so by the 2018 Navtej Johar judgment.

items.headline: Supreme Court issues guidelines on habeas corpus and protection pleas by LGBTQ+ people
items.summary: In a 11 March judgment on a Kerala lesbian woman's appeal, a bench led by the Chief Justice called attempts to change a person's orientation through counselling 'completely inappropriate'. It told judges not to substitute their own subjective values.

items.headline: Kerala lesbian couple moves High Court alleging forced 'conversion therapy' at hospital
items.summary: A couple alleged that one of them was forcefully taken from her partner and subjected to conversion therapy at a private hospital in Kozhikode. The court issued notice to the hospital; the allegations had not been tested.

items.headline: Union government forms six-member committee on queer community concerns
items.summary: As directed by the Supreme Court in the marriage equality case, the Law Ministry notified a committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary. The News Minute noted it consists only of government secretaries, though others may be added.

items.headline: Madras High Court directs horizontal reservation for transgender people in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: Justice GK Ilanthiraiyan struck down a 2015 order that classed trans persons without community certificates as MBC, ruling it violated constitutional equality provisions. The petition was filed by a trans woman nurse.
items.outcome: State directed to provide horizontal reservation in education and employment.

items.headline: Bengaluru police arrest 51-year-old woman over death of 42-year-old transgender housemate
items.summary: Police said the body of a 42-year-old transgender person was found on 3 May and a post-mortem indicated strangulation, after which a murder case was registered. The accused, a housemate of 20 years, was arrested in Hassan.
items.outcome: One arrested and charged with murder.

items.headline: Calcutta High Court orders 1% reservation for transgender people in West Bengal government services
items.summary: ThePrint reported the High Court held that mandatory reservations under the 2014 NALSA ruling had not been implemented in West Bengal. It said transgender persons must get 1% reservation in state services.

items.headline: Guwahati school allegedly asks transgender Class 11 student to leave over Instagram post
items.summary: Scroll, citing The Assam Tribune and The Wire, reported the principal allegedly told the student's mother that her child should leave the school after a swimwear photo on a private account. The principal said the school had received complaints from some parents.

items.headline: Bihar's first transwoman police sub-inspector clears recruitment test
items.summary: PTI reported that Manvi Madhu Kashyap cleared the recruitment test and became the first transwoman sub-inspector in Bihar Police. She said she had been rejected by several coaching centres for being transgender.

items.headline: Centre announces 'interim action' for queer couples on ration cards and joint bank accounts
items.summary: The Wire reported the Centre directed that partners in a queer relationship be treated as one household for ration cards, with no restriction on joint bank accounts or nominating a partner. It also provided for claiming a partner's body when no relative is available.
items.outcome: Administrative advisories issued; no change in marriage law.

items.headline: Kerala High Court orders state to implement transgender reservations within six months
items.summary: A bench issued the order on 28 November 2024, uploaded on 14 January 2025, on a trans woman's petition noting the Public Service Commission had not implemented reservations. It cited the 2014 NALSA verdict.
items.outcome: Government directed to implement within six months.

items.headline: Andhra couple allegedly die by suicide after son's wish to marry a transgender person
items.summary: Police in Nandyal said a middle-aged couple took their lives after conflicts over their 24-year-old son's relationship with a transgender person. Police said the son had previously attempted suicide over the matter.

items.headline: 44 transgender persons clear tests for Hyderabad Traffic Assistants roles
items.summary: Hyderabad Police said 44 of 58 transgender candidates cleared physical efficiency tests after the Chief Minister asked officials to engage trans persons as traffic volunteers. The move was described as recognition for the community.

items.headline: Andhra Pradesh High Court upholds lesbian couple's right to live together
items.summary: On a habeas corpus petition, the bench directed the parents of one woman not to interfere with the relationship, noting their daughter is a major. The report said police had earlier kept her at a welfare home for 15 days although she said she wished to live with her partner.

items.headline: Noida police arrest four accused of extorting people via LGBTQ dating app
items.summary: Police said the four accused, aged 19 to 22, allegedly lured victims into physical relations and then blackmailed them. A complaint was registered at Phase 3 police station.

items.headline: Supreme Court dismisses review petitions against marriage equality verdict
items.summary: A five-judge bench dismissed review petitions against the October 2023 judgment, saying it found no error apparent on the face of the record. The court said the view expressed in both judgments was in accordance with law and no interference was warranted.

items.headline: Anakapalle police probe killing of transgender person; suspects confessed, police say
items.summary: Police said body parts of a transgender person were found on the national highway and the suspects later confessed. The outlet described the case as a love triangle, per police.

items.headline: Bengaluru: 40-year-old transgender person found with stab wounds; husband sought, police say
items.summary: Police said the victim, a member of an NGO working for transgender welfare, was found at home in K R Puram. Police said the couple had frequent quarrels and a search was on for her husband; an NGO member had written to police suspecting his involvement.
items.outcome: Search for suspect under way at time of report.

items.headline: Madras High Court: same-sex couples can form a family, marriage not the sole basis
items.summary: In a 22 May order on a habeas corpus petition, a bench said that although same-sex marriage is not legalised, 'chosen family' is well settled in LGBTQIA+ jurisprudence and the petitioner and her partner can constitute a family.
items.outcome: Order in favour of the petitioner; family restrained from interfering.

items.headline: Pride march held in Delhi on 31 May 2025
items.summary: Scroll reported a march flagged off from The Lalit Hotel where participants spoke of claiming space and, for some, being out in public for the first time. The report called it a rare day of safety for many.

items.headline: Andhra Pradesh High Court: trans woman in heterosexual marriage protected under Section 498-A
items.summary: A single judge ruled that a transgender woman in a heterosexual marriage is entitled to protection from cruelty under Section 498-A IPC. The court said a narrow view of womanhood undermines constitutional dignity.

items.headline: Kerala High Court allows trans couple to be named 'parents' on child's birth certificate
items.summary: The court ordered that the couple, whose baby was born in February 2023, be listed as 'parents' rather than 'father' and 'mother'. PTI described the verdict as the first of its nature in the country.

items.headline: Chennai Rainbow Pride March draws more than 10,000 participants
items.summary: The News Minute reported the 17th edition took place at Rajarathinam Stadium in Egmore. Held annually at the end of June, it is dedicated to the political and personal rights of the LGBTQIA+ community.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu releases State Policy for Transgender Persons 2025; groups call it unambitious
items.summary: The Social Welfare department released the policy on 31 July after a drafting process of about three years. Trans rights groups criticised the absence of horizontal reservation and the lack of specific implementation mechanisms.

items.headline: Kerala police bust four-member gang that extorted LGBTQ+ people via Grindr
items.summary: Police said the gang posed as romantic prospects and extorted lakhs of rupees from hundreds of people, mostly from the LGBTQ+ community. A victim's complaint over an extorted gold chain and ring led to the arrests.

items.headline: Trans person found dead in east Delhi; police probe ex-husband's alleged role
items.summary: PTI reported a transperson was found dead under a bridge in Madhu Vihar and a minor caught at the scene claimed the victim's ex-husband was responsible. Police said the minor's own role was under investigation.
items.outcome: Investigation ongoing at time of report.

items.headline: Karnataka High Court bars 'strip-and-search' method in state transgender survey
items.summary: On a PIL, a division bench restrained officials from identifying transgender people by strip-and-search during the ongoing survey and said participation must be voluntary. The order was interim, until the next hearing.
items.outcome: Interim restraint on the method; participation to be voluntary.

items.headline: Supreme Court holds schools and governments accountable over dismissal of trans teacher
items.summary: A two-judge bench delivered a judgment on 17 October on a trans teacher dismissed from private schools in Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat, criticising Centre and states for not implementing the 2019 Act and 2020 Rules. ThePrint reported compensation of Rs 2 lakh in total was awarded.
items.outcome: Rs 50,000 each from the Centre, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and a Gujarat private school.

items.headline: Kerala High Court directs two extra law college seats for transgender students
items.summary: Justice VG Arun's interim order of 24 October came on a petition from a candidate seeking admission under a transgender category at Kozhikode Government Law College.

items.headline: Hyderabad Metro appoints 20 transgender persons as security personnel
items.summary: The metro operator said the staff began duty on 1 December after induction training, at selected stations and inside trains. It described the move as in line with the state's commitment to inclusivity.

items.headline: Thousands join Bengaluru Pride march from Kanteerava Stadium
items.summary: Deccan Herald reported students, trans communities, queer collectives and international visitors marched with slogans and music, highlighting both celebration and ongoing demands for rights.

items.headline: Ballia: man found hanging after allegedly killing 65-year-old transgender woman, police say
items.summary: PTI reported the woman went missing and community members filed a missing persons complaint; police said a 30-year-old man was later found hanging after allegedly killing her. The SP addressed reporters on the case.

items.headline: Odisha police: main accused in transgender person's killing injured in encounter
items.summary: PTI reported that a transgender person was found fatally injured near Uttara Chowk on the Bhubaneswar-Puri highway on 1 February and was declared dead at hospital. Police said a 25-year-old identified as the prime accused was injured in a police encounter in Puri district.
items.outcome: Police said the prime accused was injured in an encounter in Puri district.

items.headline: Delhi Queer Pride march held from Barakhamba to Jantar Mantar
items.summary: ThePrint reported the march ended at Jantar Mantar with performances. A debate over 'respectability' arose when organisers stopped a dancer's performance mid-way.

items.headline: Queer woman leaving marital home faced crowd at Delhi police station, report says
items.summary: The Wire's queerbeat reported that over a dozen people, identified by those present as Bajrang Dal members, surrounded Fatehpuri Beri police station while a queer woman recorded a statement that she had left her abusive marital family voluntarily. Her marital family had filed a missing-person complaint in Uttar Pradesh.

items.headline: Activist Grace Banu opposes Transgender Amendment Bill 2026 ahead of Parliament vote
items.summary: In an interview with The Wire, Dalit and transgender rights activist Grace Banu said she strongly opposed the proposed amendment to the 2019 Act. The report said the Bill, which redefines who counts as transgender, had led to protests across the country.

items.headline: UN human rights office criticises India's amended transgender law
items.summary: After the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026 received presidential assent, the UN human rights office warned it risks 'setting back hard-won rights' by replacing self-identification with mandatory medical verification. It also flagged the speed of passage without adequate consultation.

items.headline: Hundreds protest Transgender Amendment Bill 2026 at Bengaluru's Freedom Park
items.summary: The protest was called by the National Network for Gender and Sexual Minorities with activists from 18 Karnataka districts. They alleged the amendment would narrow who is recognised as a transgender person and dilute rights.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes Transgender Persons Amendment Bill 2026 amid opposition walkout
items.summary: ThePrint reported the bill, passed by voice vote, removes the right to self-identify gender and replaces it with a medical board and District Magistrate process. The government argued it protects a vulnerable community, while the transgender community argued it dismantles rights.
items.outcome: Passed by Lok Sabha by voice vote; later passed by Rajya Sabha and assented to (per other reports).

items.headline: Human Rights Watch: India's transgender rights bill a 'huge setback'
items.summary: HRW said Parliament passed a bill that changes how transgender people are legally recognised and removes the right to self-identification, and urged the President not to sign. It also raised concern about the risk of wrongful prosecution.

items.headline: Parliament clears trans amendment bill; Supreme Court-appointed panel asks Centre to withdraw it
items.summary: Scroll reported the bill passed the Lok Sabha on Tuesday and the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, and that a Supreme Court-appointed advisory committee headed by Justice Asha Menon wrote asking for its withdrawal, citing The Indian Express. Transgender, intersex and gender-diverse organisations had been protesting.
items.outcome: Bill sent to the President for assent.

items.headline: President assents to Transgender Amendment Bill; Amnesty calls it a serious setback
items.summary: Amnesty International said President Droupadi Murmu gave assent to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026, which it said denies people the right to self-identify. Amnesty India's board chair said identity must now be verified by authorities.
items.outcome: Amendment Act in force; challenged in Supreme Court.

items.headline: Rajasthan High Court calls transgender amendment a 'departure' from constitutional baseline
items.summary: A division bench, ruling on trans reservations in Public Service Commissions, remarked that conditioning legal recognition of gender identity on administrative certification departs from what the Supreme Court recognised. ThePrint said it was the first court to comment on the amendment.

items.headline: Trans activists move Supreme Court against Transgender Amendment Act 2026
items.summary: Two transgender women who are nominated members of the National Council for Transgender Persons filed an 886-page petition on 3 April. It argues the amendment violates Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21.
items.outcome: Pending; Supreme Court to hear on 4 May.

items.headline: Karnataka High Court orders hormone therapy to continue for two trans petitioners
items.summary: Petitioners challenging the 2026 amendment said doctors at a private Bengaluru hospital were unwilling to continue their mid-course therapy. The court directed the treatment continue, subject to the outcome of the writ petition and any Supreme Court orders.

items.headline: Supreme Court stays High Court challenges to Transgender Amendment Act, seeks single forum
items.summary: A bench led by the Chief Justice stayed proceedings in the Rajasthan, Delhi, Karnataka and Kerala High Courts and issued notice on the Union's transfer plea. The Solicitor General argued parallel proceedings could lead to conflicting decisions.
items.outcome: Proceedings in four High Courts stayed.

items.headline: Supreme Court says 2026 amendment does not by default invalidate existing transgender cards
items.summary: Scroll, citing The Hindu, reported the court verbally clarified the amendments will not retrospectively cancel transgender cards issued under the earlier law. Petitioners had contended the changes give the government complete power to determine gender identity.

items.headline: Centre tells Supreme Court gender self-identification could make 169 statutory provisions unworkable
items.summary: The Wire reported a three-judge bench led by the Chief Justice heard the challenge to the 2026 amendment on 3 August. The court orally asked the Centre to consider the impact on people mid-way through gender-affirming therapy or holding cards issued under the earlier law.
items.outcome: Hearing continued; no final ruling reported.

items.headline: Allahabad High Court orders UP police to protect lesbian couple threatened by relatives
items.summary: Justice Gautam Chaudhary said the two adult women were free to live together without interference after speaking to them. The state's counsel argued same-sex relationships are not accepted as they affect the social fabric, according to the report.

items.headline: Delhi High Court asks Centre, police to frame SOP on arresting transgender persons
items.summary: A bench asked authorities to take steps toward a standard operating procedure on arrest and detention of transgender people while issuing notice on a law student's PIL. The petition said Delhi Police's standing order on arrests is silent on trans persons and cited NHRC advisory issued in May.

items.headline: Centre tells Delhi High Court adults can nominate queer partners for medical decisions
items.summary: The Health Ministry and NMC said in a counter affidavit that allowing an adult to nominate a partner, including in a non-heterosexual relationship, to take medical decisions is capable of being accommodated within the existing legal framework. An opinion piece later reported the affidavit was said to be 'under objections' in court.
items.outcome: Case pending before Delhi High Court.

items.headline: Telangana Assembly passes bill to co-opt transgender persons in municipal corporations
items.summary: The Telangana Municipalities (Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2026 provides for co-option of transgender persons in nine municipal corporations outside Hyderabad's core urban region. The minister said it would give representation in municipal decision-making.

items.headline: Bengaluru Police issue guidelines to curb alleged unlawful activity by some transgender persons
items.summary: Police said the guidelines follow public complaints about aggressive solicitation, traffic obstruction and extortion, while directing personnel to safeguard trans people's rights and dignity. Community groups later demanded withdrawal.

items.headline: Bengaluru trans groups demand withdrawal of police guidelines and halt to anti-beggary drive
items.summary: Trans Feminist Collective and Naaveddhu Nilladiddare passed a resolution at a community consultation saying the guidelines reinforce stereotypes. They argued unlawful acts should be dealt with under existing laws.

items.headline: Allahabad High Court: transwoman not a 'woman' under BNS Section 69, grants bail
items.summary: In a 15 October bail order, a single judge held a transgender woman cannot be classified as a 'woman' under the BNS section on sex by deceitful means. The complainant, a Bareilly-based transwoman, alleged the accused took more than Rs 5 lakh and then refused marriage; the court distinguished other High Courts' rulings.

unconfirmed: Honour-related violence or killings of same-sex couples: searches surfaced only heterosexual honour-killing cases; no verified same-sex case from the listed outlets was found.
Landlord evictions of named trans or queer tenants after complaints to police: only general reports on rental discrimination were found, no verified individual case.
Child-kidnapping rumour lynchings other than Hyderabad (May 2018) and Thiruvananthapuram (Feb 2018): not verified.
Death of a trans woman in Kozhikode (March 2019): the community suspected foul play but the article gave no cause of death, so it was left out.
Chitradurga (Karnataka, Oct 2026): police booked two trans persons on a father's complaint of forced surgery; the report is entirely allegation against trans persons and was not included.
Supreme Court hearing of 17 August 2026 on existing transgender cards: a search summary said the Centre told the court cards would stay operational, but the article was not opened.
Palghar (Maharashtra, 2025) mob beating of four people including three men posing as transgender: victims were not trans people, so excluded.

Punjab, Bihar and Rajasthan: no verified LGBTQ-specific violence or protection-order cases from the listed outlets; Bihar and Rajasthan appear only through a police-recruitment milestone and a High Court remark on the 2026 Act.

Hindustan Times, The Hindu, Indian Express, Times of India, BBC, Guardian, Reuters and AP could not be opened by the research tools, so no entry cites them; some entries relay their reporting second-hand (named in the summary).
Conversion-therapy convictions or prosecutions: none found; entries are court orders, regulator rulings and complaints.
